correctness.rationale: For n at least 5 the graph is cubic and triangle-free. A first-force argument rules out every set of size at most 3. For size 4, choosing an actual first force reduces the local geometry to rail-rail or rail-rung. In either case, after that force a second force exists only when the fourth initial blue vertex occupies one of four explicitly listed local positions; these are exactly types A-D. Constructive forcing sequences show all A-D sets succeed, and disjoint counting gives 13n. The direct checker verifies all subsets of size at most 4 for n=5 through 11.

value.rationale: The result gives the complete optimum-configuration space on a canonical cubic family, not merely a scalar recomputation. Minimum zero forcing sets are the vertices of the zero forcing reconfiguration graph, so their exact classification is directly structural. The four local types and 13n multiplicity support reconfiguration and optimal-placement questions and are not implied by the known scalar minimum.
